chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated from Hameed ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Sabah, from Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadhrami, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ishaq ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of the Exalted: 'And if We delay punishment from them until a numbered period: they will surely say,

And if We delay punishment from them until a numbered period: they will surely say, "What is detaining it? Indeed, when it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and that which they used to mock will encompass them."
He said: The punishment is the rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him), and the numbered period is the number of the people of Badr and his companions.

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَدْرٍ: The people of Badr (the companions of the Prophet at the battle of Badr)
key_terms.الْعَذَابُ: The punishment (interpreted here as the rise of the Imam)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser (a title for the Twelfth Imam, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'numbered period' in the verse about the delay of punishment?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the 'delayed punishment' in Surah Fussilat is interpreted eschatologically as the period of occultation or pre-emergence of the Qa'im, where humanity grows impatient for divine justice. The specific identification of the 'numbered period' with the 313 companions of Badr establishes a symbolic parallel, suggesting that the Qa'im's army will mirror the fidelity and number of the Prophet's earliest supporters, a key motif in Shia eschatology. This interpretation underscores the continuity between the Prophetic era and the Mahdi's revolution, framing the delay not as absence but as a calculated divine timing.
